title: Why is there such a string focus on losing weight?
body: I used to use this app for a while and it worked okay, but stopped working out and tried to redownload it. Why. Is. There. Such. A. Strong. Emphasis. On. Weight. Loss!? You can’t even log in and use the app without setting a weight loss goal! Every single exercise comes with a note on how much weight you’ll lose. I understand it’s useful if you ARE trying to lose weight, but the app SPECIFICALLY ASKS what your goals are (disappointed to find out that increasing flexibility wasn’t an option, but I guess it’s a little niche) and never once did I include weight loss. I think it’s toxic (and this is more critique of diet culture as whole rather than the app itself) to assume every goddamn person tying to stay fit is trying to lose weight. I just want to be healthy, not feel pressured into losing weight when I’m already at a healthy one. And, in the end, I don’t particularly care too much, I just deleted the app again, but what about the teenagers using this app? (There is a specific option when you log in to state you are under 18.) I don’t think it’s healthy to subject teenagers to that constant pressure, or worse, someone who has already struggled with EDs or an obsession with weight loss/appearance. It’s one thing for the option to be there, in fact, I think it’s great for those who need or want it, but the way that this is constantly shoved down your throat is ridiculous. The creators are (or at should be) fully aware that losing weight isn’t the only reason to work out, so why don’t they act like it?
